title: Learning to walk with crutches and walkers
what: A specialist fits crutches, a walker or a cane to your height and teaches you to use them correctly. Walking becomes safer and easier.
why: After a leg injury or operation, with weakness, after a stroke, and for older people at risk of falling.
tell_doctor: Whether you may put weight on the sore leg, and how much
Whether you have dizziness or falls
Pain or weakness in the arms and shoulders
What stairs and thresholds you have at home

prepare.title: Aids
prepare.text: If you already have crutches or a walker, bring them. They will be adjusted to your height.

prepare.title: Shoes
prepare.text: Closed shoes with a non-slip sole and a heel counter.

prepare.title: Home
prepare.text: Remove rugs and cords from the floor and clear the walkways.

bring: Crutches, a walker or a cane, if you have them
Discharge papers with the doctor's instructions
steps: The specialist adjusts the height of the aid to your height
Teaches you to stand up from a chair and sit down using the aid
Shows the order of steps: aid first, then the sore leg, then the healthy leg
Teaches you to go up and down stairs
Gives tips on making your home safer
feel: At first it feels strange and your arms tire quickly
You may be afraid of falling. The specialist will be right next to you
after: Practice a little, several times a day
Replace the rubber tips when they wear down
Do not carry things in your hands. Use a backpack or a shoulder bag
red_flags: You fell and your leg hurts a lot
Pain and numbness in the armpits from crutches: the height is wrong

faq.q: How do I use stairs with crutches?
faq.a: Going up, the healthy leg goes first; going down, the crutches and the sore leg go first. The specialist will show you.

faq.q: Which is better, crutches or a walker?
faq.a: A walker is steadier; crutches are faster and easier on stairs. The specialist will choose.

reminders.text: Walking training today. Bring your crutches or walker and comfortable shoes.
